questions.stem: SVR s. 404 says no person shall operate a passenger-carrying vessel of the Part 4 class:
options: in circumstances beyond its design limitations
in winter without a special operating permit
without a written forecast on board
in fog without a radar reflector
questions.explanation: It also says the vessel shall be designed and equipped to operate safely in its area of operation.

questions.stem: Which regulation extends the same two duties to workboats?
options: SVR s. 404 only
MPR s. 216
SVR s. 501
questions.explanation: Section 501 says a workboat shall be designed and equipped to operate safely in its area of operation and not operated beyond its design limitations.

questions.stem: Who must provide a document setting out a vessel's design limitations to the end user?
options: The master of the vessel
The weather office for the area
The builder, manufacturer, rebuilder or importer
The Coast Guard marine safety office
questions.explanation: SVR s. 717(4); the limits include capacity, power and environmental limitations.

questions.stem: There is no weather warning in effect. A 9 m passenger boat has a design limit of 1.5 m seas, and the forecast is 2 m seas by afternoon. What is the right conclusion?
options: Go anyway, since there is no warning in effect
The afternoon exceeds the limit: finish early or do not go
Go, but stay close to shore so the limit does not apply
Wait for a gale warning before deciding
questions.explanation: The vessel's limit applies whether or not there is a warning.

questions.stem: A master meets force 10 with no storm warning received. Under CSA 2001 s. 112 the master must:
options: warn nearby vessels and the authorities ashore
do nothing, as no warning was issued
only note it in the official log book later
only call the owner by phone

questions.stem: Why plan to arrive at a pass at slack water when strong wind is forecast against the flow?
options: Slack water increases the current through the pass
Wind and current never interact in a pass
It saves fuel, but it makes no difference to the sea state
Wind against current steepens the sea; slack lowers the risk
questions.explanation: Seas steepen where wind opposes current; passes can be navigable at slack but not at peak flow.

questions.stem: At what local times should the latest forecast be checked for a day plan?
options: Only at midnight, the night before
Only at noon on the day
At the issue times 04:00, 10:30, 16:00 and 21:30
Never; once a day is enough
questions.explanation: Check before departure and before any exposed leg.

questions.stem: Which sequence is the best order for a weather go/no-go?
options: Fuel price, hull colour, then warnings
Warnings, winds, sea, tide, local effects, limits, shelter, light, comms, turn-back
Crew preference, then the forecast, then luck
Vessel colour, wind, then the tide
questions.explanation: The checklist in the lesson is a teaching tool, not an official procedure.

questions.stem: A forecast says 'wind light' for the area but the route passes an inlet mouth on a summer morning. What should you consider?
options: An outflow could give strong wind at the mouth
Nothing, because light means light everywhere
A tsunami warning for the inlet
That the tide will be higher than usual
questions.explanation: Outflow and inflow winds in inlets can exceed the regional forecast.

questions.stem: Which warning category and range is correct for gale and storm?
options: Gale 20 to 33; storm 34 to 47
Gale 48 to 63; storm 64 or more
Gale 28 to 33; storm 34 to 40
Gale 34 to 47 knots; storm 48 to 63 knots
